auditType: post-hoc independent source and retained trace review
scope: All 32 completed episodes; no controller contact, reruns, source changes, or outcome filtering.
supportedInterpretation: Model-generated dependency plans completed serial tool workflows with fewer submitted model decisions than the defined one-operation-per-decision ReAct controller in both interface arms.
Both implementations completed all tested stable, rebinding, stale-state and fresh-handoff cases. No success advantage attributable to Interego was observed.
The Interego composition performed more backend reads in this local component experiment. These are actual counted reads, not production network latency or dollar cost.
limits: Provider inference calls, tokens, dollar cost and exact model snapshot were unavailable; submitted decisions are not an API-call or token measurement.
The two seeds select initial-state and key fixtures. There is one episode per scenario/controller/interface/initial-state cell, not repeated stochastic trials of an identical cell.

The adapter supplies equivalent task information and opaque controls. Binding values, key ordering and error wording differ. Raw MCP ergonomics, integration effort and general capability discovery were not measured.
Observed dependency plans were serial; this run supplies no evidence of parallel speedup or runtime branching advantages.
Registry success/failure priors are synthetic fixture data. No procedure learning, cross-episode reuse or performance of the brother's unseen implementation was measured.
Fresh-agent identity/fork settings are recorded in the provider sidecar; exact host inference telemetry is unavailable.
This audit checks retained traces, board transitions and source consistency. Independent reconstruction and cryptographic verification of the signed descriptor envelopes is a separate audit.
